modules.name: Cell theory, Cell Membrane and Cell Wall

blocks.title: Cell Theory
blocks.text:
CELL

  • Cell is a structural and functional unit of life.
Unicellular organisms are capable of :

(i) independent existence

(ii) performing all functions of life

anything less than a complete structure of cell does not ensure independent existence/living.

Cell Theory :

Cell theory: Proposed by Schleiden and Schwann

Schleiden: All plants are made up of different types of cells which form plant tissues.

Schwann:

• The bodies of plants and animals are composed of cell and cell products
    • Schleiden and Schwann were not able to describe how new cells were formed.

Final shape to cell theory: Rudolf Virchow

Cell theory:

(1) All living organisms are made up of cells and cell products.

(2) New cells arise from pre-existing cells.

blocks.title: Cell Membrane
blocks.text:
• Biochemical investigation clearly revealed that the cell membranes possess lipid, protein and carbohydrates.
  • Human erythrocyte membrane has approximately 52% protein and 40% lipids.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question:
Q.1 Which of the following are not membrane-bound?

(1) Mesosomes

(2) Vacuoles

(3) Ribosomes

(4) Lysosomes
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

Ribosomes are organelles that float freely in the cytoplasm and do not require a membrane to perform their functions.

blocks.question:
The concept of "Omnis cellula-e cellula" regarding cell division was first proposed by:

(1) Rudolf Virchow

(2) Theodore Schwann

(3) Schleiden

(4) Aristotle
blocks.answer:

The concept of "Omnis cellula-e cellula" regarding cell division was first proposed by Rudolf Virchow in 1855.

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.question:
Cellular organelles with membranes are :

(1) Lysosomes, Golgi apparatus and mitochondria

(2) Nuclei, ribosomes and mitochondria

(3) Chromosomes, ribosomes and endoplasmic reticulum

(4) Endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes and nuclei.
blocks.answer:
Ans- 1

The cellular organelles with membranes are lysosomes, Golgi apparatus, and mitochondria:

  • Lysosomes
These organelles are bound by a single membrane and contain digestive enzymes that break down excess or worn out organelles, food particles, viruses, bacteria, and macromolecules.
  • Golgi apparatus
This organelle is bound by a single membrane and is made up of folded and flattened membranes that help with intracellular transport and secretion.
  • Mitochondria
These organelles are bound by a double membrane and are known as the "powerhouse" of the cell. They are found in all eukaryotic cells and produce energy in the form of ATP.

blocks.title: Core Concepts: Endo Membrane
blocks.text:
1. Definition and introduction

  • The membranous organelles are distinct in terms of their structure and function; many of these are considered together as an endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated.
  • The endomembrane system includes the Endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles because their functions are coordinated.
2. Endoplasmic Reticulum:

blocks.title: 4. Lysosome:
blocks.text:
• These are membrane bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.

  • Very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases-lipases, proteases, carbohydrases and nucleases) optimally active at the acidic pH (pH=5).
  • Lysosomes are highly polymorphic cell organelles. Because lysosomes have different physiological states.
  • These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

blocks.title: Exercise: 3 Endo Membrane System
blocks.question:
Q.3: Which of the following statements is not correct?

(1) Lysosomes have numerous hydrolytic enzymes.

(2) The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH.

(3) Lysosomes are membrane-bound structures.

(4) Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum.
blocks.answer:
Ans.-4

The statement that is not correct is "Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum". Instead, lysosomes bud off from the trans face of Golgi bodies. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) synthesizes the precursors of lysosomal enzymes, which are then sent to the Golgi bodies for further processing.
options: (2) The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH.
(4) Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum.

blocks.title: Exercise : 4
blocks.question:
Q.4 Which of the following are NOT considered as the part of endomembrane system ?

A. Mitochondria

B. Endoplasmic Reticulum

C. Chloroplasts

D. Golgi complex

E. Peroxisomes

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

(1) A, C and E only

(2) A and D only

(3) A, D and E only

(4) B and D only
blocks.answer:
Ans- 1

The endomembrane system includes endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Peroxisomes, mitochondria and chloroplasts do not have their functions coordinated; hence, they are not part of the endomembrane system.

blocks.text:
Chloroplast:

• The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis.

• Granum acts as the site of light reaction.

  • The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates. (i.e. enzymes of Calvin cycle or Dark reaction) and proteins.

Microbodies:
Many membrane bound minute vesicles called microbodies that contain various enzymes are present in both plant and animal cells.

NUCLEUS:

Chromosome:-

Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types.
      • The metacentric chromosome has a  middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome.

    • The sub-metacentric chromosome has a centromere nearer to one end of the chromosome, resulting in one shorter arm and one longer arm.
    • In the case of an acrocentric chromosome, the centromere is situated close to its end, forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
    • The telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.

blocks.answer:

The structures that are formed by stacking of organized flattened membranous sacs in the chloroplasts are grana.

blocks.question:
Q.2 The chromosomes in which the centromere is situated close to one end are:

(1) Acrocentric

(2) Telocentric

(3) Sub-metacentric

(4) Metacentric
blocks.answer:
Ans-1

Acrocentric chromosomes have a centromere that is located near one end of the chromosome, resulting in one very short arm and one very long arm. Acrocentric chromosomes often have satellites, which are small club-like bodies that are connected to the short arms of the chromosome.

blocks.title: Exercise 3
blocks.question:
Q.3 Microtubules are the constituents of:

(1) Cilia, Flagella and Peroxisomes

(2) Spindle fibres, Centrioles and Cilia

(3) Centrioles, Spindle fibres and Chromatin

(4) Centrosome, Nucleosome and Centrioles
blocks.answer:
Ans.-2

Microtubules are constituents of spindle fibers, centrioles, and cilia:

  • Cilia
Microtubules are part of the structure and function of cilia, which are hair-like structures that help organisms move. Cilia are found in many types of eukaryotic cells, and are often used for locomotion in unicellular organisms.
  • Flagella
Microtubules are part of the structure and function of flagella, which are hair-like structures that help organisms move. Flagella are found on sperm cells and many protozoans.
  • Spindle fibers
Microtubules form spindle fibers, which are essential during cell division. Centrioles form the spindle fibers that give rise to the spindle apparatus during cell division.
  • Centrioles
Centrioles are involved in organizing microtubules. Centrioles are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin.

blocks.title: Exercise 5
blocks.question:
Q.5 Assertion (A) : Chloroplast & Mitochondria are considered as "Semi-autonomous organelle" of the cell.

Reason (R) : Both the organelle possess their own genetic material and have their own protein synthesising machinery.

(1) Both Assertion and Reason are True and the Reason is a correct explanation of the Assertion.

(2) Both Assertion and Reason are True but Reason is not a correct explanation of the Assertion.

(3) Assertion is True but the Reason is False.

(4) Both Assertion and Reason are False.
blocks.answer:
Ans- 1

Mitochondria and chloroplasts are considered semi-autonomous organelles because they have their own DNA and protein-synthesizing machinery. They can synthesize some of their own proteins, but they still depend on the nucleus for other proteins.
options: (A) : Chloroplast & Mitochondria are considered as "Semi-autonomous organelle" of the cell.
(1) Both Assertion and Reason are True and the Reason is a correct explanation of the Assertion.
(2) Both Assertion and Reason are True but Reason is not a correct explanation of the Assertion.
(3) Assertion is True but the Reason is False.
(4) Both Assertion and Reason are False.
